Rashi on Pesachim 95a:10:1.hebrew: ואין לי - שיהא כלל מוסיף אלא על הפרט של עשה — מצות ומרורים — דכוותיה צלי אש, שהוא מ"ע. ופרט נמי ממעט דכוותיה — השבתת שאור:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:10:1.english: And I have [derived] only - That the generalization adds only [mitzvot similar] to the specific [case] of a positive [mitzvah] — matzot and bitter herbs — [namely,] what is like it, [such as eating it] roasted over fire, which is a positive mitzvah. And the specific [case] also excludes [something] like it — [namely,] the removal of leaven.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:10:2.hebrew: ל"ת מנין - שירבה הכלל, וכן הפרט ימעט ל"ת. ת"ל לא ישאירו ממנו עד בקר, וכתיב כללא לאהדורי עליה לרבויי דכוותיה — לאו הניתק לעשה — ולמעט בפרטיה לא יראה ולא ימצא, דלאו שניתק לעשה נינהו, כדמפרש במסקנא:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:10:2.english: From where [do we derive] a negative commandment - [Meaning,] which [negative commandment] the generalization includes, and similarly [which] negative commandment the specification excludes. The verse states: "They shall leave none of it until morning," and a generalization is written to turn back upon it to include [others] like it — a prohibition remedied by a positive commandment — and to exclude by its specification "[leaven] shall not be seen" and "[leaven] shall not be found," for they are not [prohibitions] remedied by a positive commandment, as [the Gemara] explains in the conclusion.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:11:1.hebrew: ואין לי אלא כו' ל"ת גמורה מנין - שירבה [הכלל] וימעט פרט? ת"ל: "לא ישברו", וכתב כללא לאהדורי עליה, לרבויי דכוותיה בכללא ולמעוטי דכוותיה בפרטא, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:11:1.english: And I have only, etc., a full-fledged negative [mitzva], from where [is it derived] - That the generalization should include [it] and a specification should exclude [accordingly]? The verse states: "[They] shall not break [a bone in it]"; and it wrote a generalization to go back over it, to include what is similar to it through the generalization and to exclude [what is not] similar to it through the specification, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:12:1.hebrew: בפרטיה מאי קא ממעט - דכל פרטא משמע מיעוטא דכוותיה, דהכי משמע: האי ולא מידי אחרינא. השבתת שאור, דהויא נמי כמצות עשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:12:1.english: Through its detail, what does it exclude - For every detail implies an exclusion of something similar to it, for it implies thus: "this, and nothing else." [It excludes] the removal of leaven, which is also like a positive commandment.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:12:2.hebrew: <abbr title="לא תעשה">ל"ת</abbr> דמותיר לאו הניתק לעשה הוא, דכתיב גבי ראשון והנותר ממנו וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:12:2.english: The negative commandment of leaving over [meat] is a prohibition that is rectified by a positive commandment, as it is written regarding the first [Pesach]: "And that which remains of it," etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:13:1.hebrew: לא תוציא - לאו הניתק לעשה הוא, דכתיב: בבית אחד יאכל לא תוציא וגו', ומשמע: לא תוציא לאוכלו, אלא בבית אחד יאכל — בעמוד והחזר קאי אם הוציאו. ולית ליה להאי תנא הא דתני בכיצד צולין (שם): האוכלו הרי זה בל"ת דובשר בשדה טרפה (שמות כ״ב:ל׳), אלא מותר להחזירו ולאוכלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:13:1.english: You shall not remove - It is a prohibition rectified by a positive commandment, as it is written: "In one house shall it be eaten; you shall not remove, etc.," and this implies: do not remove [it] to eat it [outside], rather "in one house shall it be eaten" — [meaning] it is subject to [the positive commandment of] "arise and return [it]" if one removed it. And this Tanna does not hold of that which is taught in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (there): one who eats it is [in violation of] the prohibition of "and flesh in the field, torn [by beasts]" (Exodus 22:30); rather, it is permitted to return it and eat it.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:14:1.hebrew: ולא יראה - ואם נראה, תשביתוהו; לעולם הוא בעמוד והשבת כל ימות המועד:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:14:1.english: And it shall not be seen - And if it is seen, you shall remove it; one is always [subject to] "arise and remove [it]" all the days of the festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:15:1.english: Through the generalization of "they shall not break a bone in it" - Which includes a full negative commandment.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:1:1.hebrew: מצה וחמץ יש לו בבית - בגמ' יליף לה לטעמא דכולה מתניתין:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:1:1.english: Matzah and chametz he has in the house - In the Gemara, it derives the reason for the entire Mishnah.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:2:1.english: According to all the statute of the Paschal lamb, etc. - [This] is written regarding the second Pesach.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:2:3.hebrew: במצות שבגופו הכתוב מדבר - לא ריבה את השני לדין ראשון אלא במצות שבגופו, כגון סדר עבודותיו ואכילת צלי, אבל לא למצות שאינן בגופו, כגון השבתת שאור:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:2:3.english: The verse is speaking of mitzvot [pertaining to] its body - [Scripture] only included the second [Pesach] in the law of the first with respect to mitzvot [pertaining to] its body, such as the order of its sacrificial services and eating [it] roasted, but not for mitzvot that are not [pertaining to] its body, such as the removal of leaven.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:3:1.hebrew: מצות שעל גופו מנין - כגון מצה ומרור, שהן דברים אחרים ובאין חובה לו:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:3:1.english: Mitzvot [that are] upon its body, from where [are they derived] - For example, matzah and bitter herbs, which are other things and come as an obligation for it.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:3:2.hebrew: יכול אף מצות שלא על גופו - כגון השבתת שאור. ולקמיה פריך: מנא תיתי? והאמרת "אותו" משמע מצות שבגופו:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:3:2.english: One might [have thought] even mitzvot not on its body - Such as the removal of leaven. And later [the Gemara] asks: From where would you derive [that]? Did you not say [that] "it" implies mitzvot on its body?

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:3:3.hebrew: מה שבירת העצם מיוחדת - לקמן יליף לה בפרט וכלל, דפרטי כתיבי ברישא והדר כלל: "על מצות ומרורים יאכלוהו", וכן "לא ישאירו ממנו עד בקר", "ועצם לא ישברו בו" — פרטי; "ככל חוקת הפסח יעשו אותו" — כלל. ולקמיה מפרש לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:3:3.english: Just as [the prohibition of] breaking a bone is notable - Later on, [the Gemara] derives it through a detail and a generalization, for the details are written first and then the generalization: "They shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs," and likewise "They shall not leave any of it until morning," [and] "And they shall not break a bone in it" — [these are] details; "According to all the statutes of the Paschal offering they shall make it" — [this is] a generalization. And later on, [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:4:1.hebrew: איסי בן יהודה אומר - אינו צריך לא ישברו לכך, אלא ללימוד אחר כדלקמן, דאותו מצות שבגופו משמע:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:4:1.english: Isi ben Yehuda says - [The phrase] "they shall not break [a bone]" is not needed for this [derivation], but rather for another derivation, as [stated] below; for [the word] "it" [in "they shall perform it"] implies mitzvot [pertaining] to its body.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:5:1.english: But you said - We read [the text as]: "'it' [refers to] mitzvot applicable to its body."

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:1.hebrew: ה"ק - השתא דכתיב מצות ומרורים, ואיתרבי מצוה שאינה גופו, אלמא אותו לאו דוקא:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:1.english: This is what [the baraita] is saying - Now that it is written, "unleavened bread and bitter herbs," and a mitzvah that is not [performed on] its body is included, apparently [the word] "it" is not specific.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:2.english: And it would be a detail and a generalization - For the details are written first.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:3.hebrew: ואימא נעשה כלל מוסיף על הפרט - ואיתרבי כל מילי, אפילו השבתת שאור שאינה על גופו:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:3.english: And say [that] the generalization adds to the detail - And everything is included, even the removal of leaven, which is not [performed] upon its body.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:4.hebrew: קמ"ל - "ועצם לא ישברו", דלא תדרוש כלל מוסיף על הפרט לרבויי כל מילי, אפי' השבתת שאור, דאם כן כל הני פרטי למה לי? אלא להכי כתבינהו לכולהו, למידרש תוספתא דכללא אכל חד וחד, ומרבי דומיא דפרטי ותו לא. וכולהו פרטי הוו דגופו ודעל גופו, והיינו דקאמר תנא דפרטי "ועצם לא ישברו" ממעט מצות שלא על גופו, כגון "לא תשחט על חמץ", כדלקמן. ולקמן בברייתא מפרשי מאי מרבי כללא דכל חד וחד, ומאי ממעט פרטא:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:6:4.english: [Therefore, it] teaches us - [i.e., the verse] "and they shall not break a bone [in it]," so that you should not expound [it as] a generalization adding to the detail to include everything, even the removal of leaven; for if so, why do I need all these details? Rather, for this [purpose] it wrote all of them: to expound the addition of the generalization upon each and every one, so that it includes [only] things similar to the details and nothing more. And all the details are [mitzvot] of its body and upon its body; and this is what the Tanna said: that the detail "and they shall not break a bone [in it]" excludes mitzvot that are not upon its body, such as "you shall not slaughter [My sacrifice] with leaven," as [explained] below. And below in the baraita they explain what the generalization of each and every one includes, and what the detail excludes.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:7:1.hebrew: מאי עביד ליה - מככל חוקת הפסח נפקא ליה, דהא לדידיה אותו דוקא וממעט שלא על גופו, וממילא מתרבה שבירת עצם, דהא מצוה שבגופו היא. ותמיהא לי, אמאי לא בעי נמי, לא ישאירו לאיסי מאי עביד ליה, דהא מצוה שבגופו היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:7:1.english: What does he do with it - He derives it from "according to all the statutes of the Passover" [Numbers 9:12], for according to him, "it" is specific [and exclusive] and excludes [mitzvot] not [performed] on its body, and consequently [the prohibition against] breaking a bone is automatically included, for it is a commandment [performed] on its body. And it is astonishing to me: why does [the Gemara] not also ask, "What does Isi do with 'they shall not leave over,'" for that [too] is a commandment [performed] on its body.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:7:2.hebrew: מיבעי ליה אחד עצם כו' - דהכי דרשינן בכיצד צולין (לעיל פסחים דף פה.): כשהוא אומר ועצם לא ישברו בפסח שני שאין ת"ל, הוי אחד עצם כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:7:2.english: He needs it [for] both a bone, etc. - For so we expound in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (above, Pesachim 85a): when it says, "and a bone they shall not break," regarding the second Pesach, which there is no need to state, [it means] both a bone, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:8:1.hebrew: ורבנן - דאמרי אותו לאו דוקא, למאי איכתב:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:8:1.english: And the Rabbis - who say [that] "it" is not literal, for what [purpose] was it written?

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:8:2.hebrew: שאין שוחטין - פסח שני על היחיד שנדחה לו. להכי כתב יעשו לשון רבים, דכמה דאפשר לאהדורי אחר טמא חבירו להמנותו עמו, מהדרינן, כגון לטמא אחד בשרץ. ואיידי דכתיב יעשו, כתיב אותו; דאע"ג דכתיב ברישא יעשו אותו, אי לא כתביה זימנא אחריתי הוה אמינא אורחיה דקרא הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:8:2.english: That one does not slaughter - [the] second Paschal [lamb] on behalf of an individual who was deferred to it. For this [reason] it wrote "they shall make [it]" in the plural, because as much as it is possible to search for another impure [person], his fellow, to register him with him, we search [for him], such as rendering one [person] impure with a creeping creature. And since it is written "they shall make," it writes "it"; for even though it is written in the first [part] "they shall make it," had it not written it another time, I would have said [that] it is [merely] the style of Scripture.

Rashi on Pesachim 95a:9:1.hebrew: ת"ל על מצות ומרורים וגו' - והדר כתיב כללא עליה, לרבויי דומיא דידיה. וכל מילי לא אמרינן דנירבי, דא"כ כל הני פרטי למה לי? ופרטא ממעט דכוותיה, כדמפרש לקמן, דכללא דכל חוקת הפסח מהדרינן אכולהו פרטא, לרבויי בכל פרטא דומיא דידיה, ולמעוטי מפרט' נמי דומיא דידיה. ומחד מפרטיה ממעטינן בל יראה ובל ימצא לקמן. וברייתא רמוזי מרמזא ואזלא כללי מאי מרבו ופרטי מאי ממעטי, ודכוותיה מרבו וממעטי:
Rashi on Pesachim 95a:9:1.english: Therefore, the Torah states: "With unleavened bread and bitter herbs, etc." - And afterward, a generalization is written regarding it, to include [things] similar to it. But we do not say that it includes everything, for if so, why do I need all these details? And the detail excludes [things] corresponding to it, as [the Gemara] explains below, that we apply the generalization of "the entire statute of the Paschal lamb" back to all the details, to include in each detail [things] similar to it, and also to exclude from [each] detail [things] corresponding to it. And from one of its details we exclude "it shall not be seen" and "it shall not be found" below. And the baraita proceeds by hinting at what the generalizations include and what the details exclude, and [that] they include and exclude [things] similar to them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:12:1.hebrew: בכלליה דמצות ומרורים מאי קמרבי צלי אש - משמע משום מצות ומרורים דקאי כללא עליה מרבינן צלי אש. ותימה: כיון דפרט וכלל הוא, בלא מצות ומרורים מרבינן צלי אש וכל מילי, אפילו השבתת שאור, ומפרטי ממעטי מכל חד וחד חדא מילתא, כדאמר בריש מרובה (ב"ק דף סב:) דמסיק: "על כל דבר פשע" — כלל ריבויא, וכל הני פרטי למה לי? חד למעוטי עבדים כו'. ויש לומר, דודאי בלא מצות ומרורים ידעינן צלי אש מכללא, ומצות ומרורים לא אתא אלא למעוטי השבתת שאור; ולא נקט האי לישנא "בכלליה דמצות ומרורים מאי קמרבי צלי אש", אלא משום דבעי למיפרך "ואיפוך אנא":
Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:12:1.english: "Through the generalization of unleavened bread and bitter herbs, what does it include? Roasting in fire" - This implies that because of "unleavened bread and bitter herbs," upon which the generalization rests, we include "roasting in fire." And this is puzzling: since it is a [case of] detail and generalization, [even] without "unleavened bread and bitter herbs" we would include "roasting in fire" and everything [else], even the removal of leaven, and from the details we would exclude one thing from each and every one — as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of [the chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 62b), where it concludes: "'For any matter of trespass' is an inclusive generalization, and why do I need all these details? One to exclude slaves, etc." And one can say that certainly without "unleavened bread and bitter herbs" we know [to include] "roasting in fire" from the generalization, and "unleavened bread and bitter herbs" only comes to exclude the removal of leaven; and [the Gemara] only used this wording — "Through the generalization of unleavened bread and bitter herbs, what does it include? Roasting in fire" — because it wanted to ask, "Perhaps I can reverse it!"

Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:13:1.hebrew: לא תוציא מן הבית - פי' בקונט' דלאו הניתק לעשה הוא, דכתיב: "בבית אחד יאכל לא תוציא"; משמע לא תוציא לאוכלו בבית אחר, אלא "בבית אחד יאכל" בעמוד והחזר קאי אם תוציאו. וקשה לר"י: היכי חשבינן ליה לאו הניתק לעשה? והא לאו שקדמו עשה הוא, ולא חשיב לאו הניתק לעשה, כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא דמכות (דף טו.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:13:1.english: "You shall not take [any of the flesh] out of the house" - [Rashi] explains in the Kunteres that it is a prohibition rectified by a positive commandment, for it is written: "In one house shall it be eaten; you shall not take [it] out"; this implies: do not take [it] out to eat it in another house, rather "in one house shall it be eaten" refers to "arise and return [it]" if you take it out. And it is difficult for Rabbi Yitzchak: how do we consider it a prohibition rectified by a positive commandment? Behold, it is a prohibition preceded by a positive commandment, and it is not considered a prohibition rectified by a positive commandment, as we say in the last chapter of Makkot (15a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:14:1.hebrew: בפרטיה קא ממעיט בל יראה - כאן משמע כמו שפירש ר"י בכל שעה (לעיל . כט:), דלא יראה הוי ניתק לעשה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:14:1.english: Through its detail, it excludes [the prohibition of] "it shall not be seen" - Here it is implied, as Ri explained in [the chapter] Bekhol Sha'ah (above, 29b), that "it shall not be seen" is [a prohibition] rectified by a positive [commandment].

Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:1:1.hebrew: מה בין ראשון לשני - בתוספ' (פרק ח) קתני נמי: הראשון נשחט בג' כיתות, ואין השני נשחט בג' כיתות. והכא תנא ושייר, דשייר נמי ביקור ד' ימים דליתיה בשני, כדאמר בגמ' (דף צו.). ובתוספתא דלא קתני ביקור — דלא קחשיב אלא הנך שנוהגין בפסח לבדו, וביקור נוהג נמי בתמיד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:1:1.english: What is [the difference] between the first [Pesach] and the second - In the Tosefta (Chapter 8) it also teaches: The first is slaughtered in three groups, and the second is not slaughtered in three groups. And here [our Mishnah] taught [some] and omitted [others], for it also omitted the four-day inspection, which does not apply on the second [Pesach], as stated in the Gemara (96a). And [as for why] the Tosefta does not teach the inspection — [it is] because it only lists those [laws] that apply to the Paschal offering alone, whereas inspection applies to the daily offering as well:

Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:7:1.hebrew: ואיסי בן יהודה עצם לא ישברו בו מאי עביד ליה - תימה: לאיסי, "לא ישאירו ממנו עד בקר" מאי עביד ליה? דהא לדידי' לא צריך למעוטי בל יראה, דמאותו מפיק מצוה שלא על גופו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:7:1.english: And Isi ben Yehuda, what does he do with "they shall not break a bone in it"? - It is astonishing: according to Isi, what does he do with "they shall leave none of it until morning"? For according to him, it is not needed to exclude [the prohibition of] "it shall not be seen" [regarding leaven], since from [the word] "it" he derives [the exclusion of] a mitzvah that is not upon its body.

Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:8:1.hebrew: מיבעי ליה שאין שוחטין את הפסח על היחיד - קשה לרשב"א: דתיפוק ליה מ"ככל חקת הפסח", וראשון נפקא לן בפרק האשה (לעיל פסחים דף צא.) דאין שוחטין אותו על היחיד מ"לא תוכל לזבוח את הפסח באחד". וי"ל: דלית ליה ההיא דרשה, ובפסח ראשון נפקא ליה משום דלא גרע מפסח שני:
Tosafot on Pesachim 95a:8:1.english: They need it [to teach] that one does not slaughter the Paschal [lamb] on [behalf of] an individual - This is difficult for the Rashba: let it be derived from "according to all the statute of the Pesach," while [for] the first [Pesach] it is derived for us in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah (above, Pesachim 91a) that one does not slaughter it on [behalf of] an individual from "You may not slaughter the Pesach within one [of your gates]." And one can answer: he does not hold of that exposition, and regarding the first Pesach, he derives it because it is no less [stringent] than the second Pesach.
